system_description.narrative_title: France unrest, political crisis and market contagion
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative is escalating civil unrest in France that has plunged the Macron government into crisis and transmitted political and financial contagion across Europe. As an open system, street protests, government fiscal choices, law‑enforcement responses, media amplification and market reactions exchange flows of information, legitimacy, capital and mobilization through reinforcing and balancing feedback loops: unrest erodes political legitimacy and depresses markets, market stress and fiscal constraints feed policy choices that can provoke further unrest, while domestic and international actors (opposition parties, insurers, investors, EU institutions) inject resources or restraints. External inputs include economic pressures (debt, fuel prices), social grievances and transnational political narratives; outputs include higher bond yields, currency moves, emergency security measures, shifts in public opinion and electoral risks.
system_description.scope: French domestic political stability and civil unrest (protests, curfews, troop deployments), government fiscal policy and debt dynamics, market impacts on French/Eurozone assets, media coverage and public opinion, and short‑term spillovers to nearby European states.
system_description.super_system: European political-economy embedded in global financial markets and transnational democratic dynamics
adjacent_subsystems: US electoral politics and the 2026 midterms
European sovereign debt and banking markets
Rise of right-wing political movements and domestic security policy

variables.name: Civil unrest intensity
variables.description: The aggregate magnitude and geographic spread of protests, riots, looting and street disorder at a given time.

variables.name: Political legitimacy
variables.description: The perceived authority and public acceptance of governing actors and policies across the population.

variables.name: Law‑enforcement response
variables.description: The intensity and tactics of policing and security deployments, including arrests, force and troop/military usage as they vary over time.

variables.name: Media amplification level
variables.description: The volume and sensationalism of media and social‑media coverage that magnifies events and signals to broader audiences.

variables.name: Public polarization
variables.description: The degree of ideological and affective division in public attitudes toward contested policies and actors.

variables.name: Government fiscal space
variables.description: The available capacity of the government to run deficits, access borrowing and finance spending without immediate market stress.

variables.name: Sovereign debt market stress
variables.description: The market pressure on sovereign borrowing conditions, reflected in spreads, yield volatility and investor risk premia.

variables.name: Capital flow volatility
variables.description: The rate and variability of cross‑border and domestic capital movements in and out of financial assets and currencies.

variables.name: Market liquidity level
variables.description: The ease with which financial assets can be bought or sold without large price concessions across affected markets.

variables.name: Mobilization capacity
variables.description: The organizational, logistical and communication ability of social movements and protest networks to recruit and deploy participants.

variables.name: Social grievance level
variables.description: The cumulative economic, social and cultural grievances motivating collective action, such as inequality, unemployment and service failures.

variables.name: Fiscal austerity pressure
variables.description: The policy and institutional push toward spending cuts, tax changes or austerity measures driven by budget constraints and market signals.

variables.name: Security measures level
variables.description: The extent of formal restrictions and emergency measures in force, including curfews, checkpoints and legal constraints on movement.

variables.name: Business disruption level
variables.description: The scale of interruptions to commercial activity, supply chains and retail operations due to unrest and security responses.

variables.name: Insurer loss expectations
variables.description: The anticipated claims and loss estimates held by insurers and financial risk‑carriers in response to property damage and civil disorder.

variables.name: Contagion pressure
variables.description: The external political and financial transmission pressure from unrest that increases the likelihood of spillovers into neighboring systems or markets.

catalysts.title: Troop deployment and weekend security surge
catalysts.description: French military and additional security forces deployed to major cities as authorities brace for a renewed wave of weekend protests.
catalysts.rationale: Reported: "France to deploy troops, admits to failures over weekend unrest"; "France to deploy military as it braces for fresh unrest this weekend".

catalysts.title: Sustained protest wave and planned demonstrations
catalysts.description: Coordinated and spontaneous protests continue with planned demonstrations across cities, sustaining high mobilization and media attention.
catalysts.rationale: "Curfews help calm France but more protests planned"; "Mass protests in France spiral into worst riots in years."

catalysts.title: Continuation of French bond sell-off
catalysts.description: Sustained sovereign bond outflows and rising yields as markets price political and social instability, raising borrowing costs and market stress.
catalysts.rationale: "French bond yields near 24-year high"; "French bond sell-off intensifies"; "French unrest compounds debt crisis fears."

catalysts.title: Extension/expansion of curfews and emergency measures
catalysts.description: Authorities extend or expand curfews and related emergency restrictions to additional cities, altering movement and enforcement rules.
catalysts.rationale: "France imposes curfews in parts of Paris, other cities"; "France extends curfews in some cities as restrictions quell unrest."

catalysts.title: Corporate guidance cuts and insurer loss recognition
catalysts.description: Companies revise earnings guidance and insurers update loss expectations as retail looting and property damage aggregate into significant claims.
catalysts.rationale: "Carrefour Slashes Guidance Due to Riots in France"; "Insurers face losses as riots in France become ‘like natural catastrophes’."

catalysts.title: Surge in far‑right political momentum
catalysts.description: Polls and prediction markets show rising odds for far‑right candidates as unrest erodes incumbents' standing, potentially reshaping electoral dynamics.
catalysts.rationale: "Prediction-market odds rise for Marine Le Pen in France 2027"; "France’s unrest lays bare 'slow agony' of Macron's twilight months."

catalysts.title: Regional tightening of anti‑riot laws and policing
catalysts.description: Neighboring European governments implement tougher anti‑riot laws and expand arrest powers in response to spillover unrest and looting.
catalysts.rationale: "Italy's Meloni approves tougher anti-riot laws after Milan violence"; "European governments warn citizens over security in France after riots."
